title: HB 291 (2011-2012 (129th General Assembly)): H. B. No. 291: Elections-restore local control/increase voter participation
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id) not stated.
(b_no_id_remedy) not stated.
(c_mail_ballot_id)
(section) 3509.03(E)
(quote) (E) One of the following: (1) The elector's driver's license number; (2) The last four digits of the elector's social security number; (3) A copy of the elector's current and valid photo identification, a copy of a military identification, or a copy of a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document, other than a notice of an election mailed by a board of elections under section 3501.19 of the Revised Code or a notice of voter registration mailed by a board of elections under section 3503.19 of the Revised Code, that shows the name and address of the elector.
(section) 3509.031(A)(5)
(quote) (5) One of the following: (a) The elector's driver's license number; (b) The last four digits of the elector's social security number; (c) A copy of the elector's current and valid photo identification, a copy of a military identification, or a copy of a current utility bill
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule) not stated.
(other) 3509.03(A): an elector may request absentee ballots by electronic mail or through the internet, if the board or Secretary of State offers internet delivery
(other) 3509.03 and 3509.031(D): a board may mail unsolicited absentee ballot applications to any registered voter; General Assembly must fund and the Secretary of State must reimburse boards in even-numbered-year general elections
(other) 3509.031: same changes for applications by members of the organized militia on active duty and their relatives
(other) note: Only one version (introduced). The ID list in 3509.03(E) and 3509.031 is reprinted existing law while the sections are amended for e-mail/internet requests and unsolicited applications. Struck words are not marked; the ID text appears unchanged.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
